approach: Write the along-incline equilibrium of the 2 kg block on the incline, using the tension found from each hanging block's own equilibrium.

steps.text: The 2 kg block hanging below the bottom pulley is in equilibrium, so the tension pulling the incline block down the slope equals its weight.
Block A hangs from the top pulley and is in equilibrium, so the tension pulling the incline block up the slope equals A's weight.
For the 2 kg block on the incline, balance the forces along the slope: the upward-pulling tension equals the downward-pulling tension plus the weight component along the slope.

common_mistakes.text: Forgetting the weight component of the 2 kg block along the slope, giving mₐ = 2 kg instead of 3 kg.
Using the full weight of the 2 kg incline block instead of only its component along the slope, giving mₐ = 2 + 2 = 4 kg.
